To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the participants identify their landscapes of fire as resilient and permanent.

insurance is an absence in landscapes of fire and that insurance is a landscaping practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people make sense of their lives, their homes and the landscapes they inhabit, in the context of climate change.
how insurance is implicated in the making and remaking of landscapes of disaster and how insurance is implicated as part of the landscape of disaster.
the ways in which insurance is being transformed through financialisation, and in particular, the role of insurance within financial markets and in the everyday lives of consumers and households.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research shows how insurance is not necessarily a permanent feature of landscapes of fire.
insurance in the landscape is contingent and that it is not a matter of insurance being more present or more absent but rather of insurance being more and less present.
insurance is not a panacea for the challenges of climate change and that insurance is not the only way to address the challenges of climate adaptation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insurance is an important tool in managing risk and in the case of climate change adaptation, it can help to mitigate losses and support resilience building.
we are interested in the ways that insurance is a part of everyday life.
insurance can be seen as a landscape of disruption, and that this disruption is not only a product of financialisation but is also a product of the landscape itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insurance is not a simple solution for climate change.
insurance is not always present in the lives of those in the most fire prone landscapes.
the role of insurance is not simply to protect people from disasters, but to help them live with them, to live with uncertainty and to live with the possibility of loss.
